title: Bean and cheese burritos
skill: Soaking and cooking dried pinto beans

notes.text: Cook the beans in the stockpot, and toast the burritos in batches.

move.title: From a bag of dried beans
move.body: A pound of dried pinto beans costs about what one can does and makes three times as much. Today you'll pick over and soak the beans the night before, simmer them gently until they're creamy all the way through, then mash them in a skillet with onion and cumin. Rolled in tortillas with rice and cheese and toasted, they're the burrito you'd buy, from scratch.

why.title: Pick them over
why.body: Dried beans are a farm crop, cleaned by machine. Now and then a small stone or a clump of dirt the same size gets through. Spread them out and look before they go in the water.

why.title: Why soak
why.body: A soaked bean has drunk water all the way to its middle, so it cooks evenly in about half the time. Unsoaked beans split on the outside while the centers stay hard. Draining the soaking water takes away some of the sugars that make beans hard to digest.

why.title: A gentle simmer
why.body: A hard boil tumbles the beans against each other and bursts their skins. A gentle simmer, with small bubbles breaking now and then, cooks them through and keeps them whole.

why.title: Salt once they soften
why.body: Salt in the pot from the start is fine for flavor, but salted early, beans can take a little longer to soften. Adding it once the skins have softened is the safe middle way.

why.title: Taste five beans
why.body: Beans in one pot don't all cook at the same speed. One soft bean doesn't mean the pot is done. When five in a row are creamy, with no chalky middle, it is.

why.title: Save the cooking liquid
why.body: The water the beans cooked in is full of their starch and flavor. A splash of it makes the mashed beans creamy without adding fat.

wrong.sign: The beans are still hard after 90 minutes
wrong.fix: Old beans take longer. Keep simmering and check every 15 minutes, adding hot water so they stay covered. Buy beans from a store that sells a lot of them.

wrong.sign: The skins split and the beans fell apart
wrong.fix: The pot boiled too hard. They're perfect for mashing. Next time, keep the bubbles small.

wrong.sign: The mashed beans are dry and stiff
wrong.fix: Stir in the bean liquid a few tablespoons at a time. They thicken as they cool, so stop while they're a little loose.
The tortilla was cold or overfilled. Warm it first, and keep the filling to a line across the lower third.

choices: To find small stones or dirt
Water reaches the middle, so they cook evenly and faster
quiz.explain: And the soaking water is thrown away.

choices: At a gentle simmer, small bubbles
At a hard boil the whole time
quiz.explain: A hard boil bursts the skins.

quiz.q: How do you know the pot of beans is done?
choices: Five beans in a row are creamy all the way through
quiz.explain: Beans in a pot cook at different speeds.

steps.text: The night before: spread the beans on the plate a handful at a time and pick out any small stones, clumps of dirt, or shriveled beans.
Put the beans in the large bowl, cover them with the soaking water, and leave them on the counter overnight, 8 to 12 hours.
steps.look: Swelled to about twice their size, with smooth skins.
steps.tip: Forgot to soak? Quick-soak: boil them in the pot for 2 minutes, turn off the heat, cover, and let them sit 1 hour.

steps.text: Drain the beans in the colander, throw away the soaking water, and rinse them under cold water.
Peel the onion and cut it in half through the root. Leave one half whole. Peel the garlic and crush each clove under the flat of the knife.
Put the beans, the cooking water, the onion half, the garlic, and the bay leaf in the large pot. Bring it to a boil over high heat.

Turn the heat down until only small bubbles break the surface now and then. Set the lid on slightly open and simmer, stirring every 20 minutes. If the beans poke above the water, add a little hot water.
steps.look: A lazy simmer: a few small bubbles, not a rolling boil.

steps.text: Taste a bean, after letting it cool. When the skin is soft and only the middle is firm, stir in the beans' salt. Keep simmering.

While the beans finish, rinse the rice in the colander until the water runs nearly clear. Put it in the saucepan with the rice's water and salt, bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low, and don't lift the lid.
steps.tip: When the timer rings, turn off the burner and leave the lid on until you need it.

steps.text: Scoop out 5 beans, let them cool, and taste them. They're done when all five are creamy all the way through, with no chalky middle. If not, keep simmering and check every 15 minutes.

target.look: Five beans in a row creamy all the way through

steps.text: Turn off the heat. Ladle 1 cup of the cooking liquid into the liquid measuring cup. Fish out the onion half and the bay leaf, and drain the beans in the colander.
steps.tip: Pour away from you; the steam rises fast.

steps.text: Cut the other onion half into ¼-inch dice.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the diced onion until soft, then stir in the cumin and chili powder for 30 seconds. Add the beans and ½ cup of the cooking liquid.

Mash the beans with the back of the fork and the wooden spoon until they're mostly smooth, with a few whole beans left. Stir in more liquid a few tablespoons at a time until they're soft and spreadable. Taste and add salt if they need it. Spoon them into the bowl, and wipe out the skillet.
steps.look: Soft and spreadable, a little looser than you want. They thicken as they cool.

steps.text: Warm each tortilla in the dry skillet over medium heat, 15 seconds a side, and stack them under a towel or a plate.

Lay a tortilla flat. Spread a line of rice, then beans, then cheese and a spoonful of salsa across the lower third, leaving 2 inches bare at each side. Fold the sides in, fold the bottom up over the filling, and roll it away from you tightly.
steps.look: A tight roll with the sides tucked in and the seam underneath.

steps.text: Set the burritos seam side down in the skillet over medium heat and toast until golden, then turn them with the tongs and toast the other side.
steps.look: Golden and crisp on both sides, sealed at the seam.

steps.text: Turn off the stove. Serve the burritos with the rest of the salsa, and sour cream if you're using it.

warm.text: Warm each corn tortilla in the dry skillet over medium heat, 20 seconds a side, and stack them under a towel or a plate.
warm.tip: Warm corn tortillas bend. Cold ones crack when you fold them.

roll.text: Lay a tortilla flat. Spread a spoonful of beans down the middle, then a little rice, cheese, and salsa. Fold it in half over the filling. Fill and fold the rest the same way.
roll.look: A neat half-moon, with the filling inside and not spilling out the edges.

toast.text: Set the tacos flat in the skillet over medium heat, as many as fit, and toast until golden, then turn them with the tongs and toast the other side. Toast the rest the same way.
toast.look: Golden and crisp on both sides, with the cheese melted inside.

serve.text: Turn off the stove. Serve the tacos with the rest of the salsa, and sour cream if you're using it.
